content: The Pennsylvania College of Optometry (PCO) is one of the most historically significant institutions in the field of optometry, having been a pioneer in both education and research throughout the 20th century. It holds the distinction of being the first optometry school in the United States to award the Doctor of Optometry degree following a comprehensive four-year educational program. Additionally, it was the first optometry school to achieve regional accreditation and to introduce courses specifically focused on contact lenses. PCO was a trailblazer in implementing interdisciplinary clinical training and establishing off-campus externship programs. It was also the first independent optometry college to develop graduate-level programs in vision rehabilitation and to form an affiliation with a medical school. The institution revolutionized its curriculum by adopting a modular approach that integrates basic sciences and clinical training. This innovative structure introduces clinical concepts, skills, and hands-on experiences early in the educational process, rather than relegating them to a post-basic studies phase. The Eye Institute (TEI) serves as the primary clinical training facility for PCO. Since its establishment, TEI has gained international recognition as a premier clinical center. It offers a wide range of services, including adult primary care, pediatric care, vision rehabilitation, laser procedures, and specialized optometry and ophthalmology services. This state-of-the-art facility operates 24 hours a day, and all PCO students begin their clinical training here early in their academic journey. Within TEI, the William Feinbloom Vision Rehabilitation Center specializes in low vision care and attracts patients from across the globe. It remains the leading research center for low vision worldwide. In addition to TEI, PCO operates two other clinical facilities in the Philadelphia area and oversees one of the largest externship programs in the United States. This program allows optometry students to gain diverse clinical experiences by rotating through private practices, community clinics, government facilities, veterans' hospitals, and Department of the Interior Indian reservation clinics, among other settings. The Elkins Park Campus of PCO is located on an 11-acre site in Cheltenham Township, Pennsylvania. This property, originally part of the Lindenhurst estate owned by John Wanamaker, was purchased in 1929 by Henry W. Breyer, Jr., who donated it to the Boy Scouts of America for use as a wildlife preserve. The site later became the home of PCO after being sold by the Philadelphia Council in 1990. The campus is situated three miles from The Eye Institute in West Oak Lane, which serves as the college's clinical classroom. The Elkins Park Campus features modern facilities and amenities, including a man-made pond that is maintained for aesthetic purposes.
